_comment: Files that ARE the artifact of a past device loss, kept deliberately as evidence.
A directory scan finds them forever, so without this list ci/check_device_loss.py
would be permanently red on an incident it did not catch live — and a check that is
always red is a check nobody reads.
This is an exclusion list, so it is the most dangerous file here. Five rules:
1. Every entry carries a reason, an owner and a date. An exclusion nobody can
review is an exclusion nobody will review.
2. Every entry carries a 'witness': the finding(s) it accounts for, by condition
and count. An exclusion that does not say what it excludes is an exclusion over
everything that file will ever say.
3. An entry naming a file that no longer exists is a FINDING (incident_record_rot),
not a silent no-op. An entry whose file yields NO finding is a FINDING
(incident_record_covers_nothing): it silences nothing today and can only blind
the check tomorrow. An entry whose file yields MORE than its witness accounts
for is a FINDING (incident_record_widened): that is a new incident hiding inside
a file that was already forgiven.
4. Excluded files are counted and printed in the frame line of every run, with
their witness. The check never says 'clean' without also saying what it did not
look at.
5. Naming a file explicitly on the command line overrides the exclusion, so the red
arm of the negative control can still read these.

records.reason: NOT an incident and not the artifact of one — the same class as device-memory-flip-gates-prediction.md above, and excluded for the same recorded reason. This is the derived census artifact written by ci/check_census_completeness.py, regenerated by the lane job itself before this screen runs. It matches because ci/census_surface_map.json's entry for the `device_losses` counter DESCRIBES the mechanism in prose — 'Sticky per-process VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST count, incremented at rust/src/vk/cmd.rs:333 on a fence wait' — and that description appears twice, once in the raw file text and once in the decoded string value. A census of our device-loss instrumentation cannot be written without naming the thing it censuses, and a detector that forces its own subject matter out of the project's writing is a detector shaping the evidence. The witness bound is what keeps this safe: if a real device-loss line is ever recorded in this generated file the count moves and incident_record_widened fires. Expect this count to MOVE when ci/census_surface_map.json rewords that entry (PR #54 edits it): the honest update there is to re-run the screen, read the new count and set it, because the finding is a quotation of our own prose and not an event. Any OTHER file in this list is the opposite case and its count must not be refreshed to clear a red.

Tank's ctx-512 KV measurement, 2026-08-02: vkWaitForFences reported VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST, work moved to the CPU EP and the process exited 0. Kept as the replayed red arm for this check, and as the artifact that exposed _verdict.FATAL_LOG_MARKERS matching nothing but our own docstring — Trinity repaired the vocabulary the same day, so this file is now the REPLAYED arm proving the repair holds (check_fatal_log exits 1 on it, quoting three lines) rather than evidence of the defect. The cause is with Switch (GQA attention loop, per-token work grows with context); this file is the record, not a new incident.

NOT an incident and not the artifact of one. This is the recorded-before-measuring prediction document for the DEVICE_MEMORY flip gates, and it QUOTES the strings `device_losses > 0` and `VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` in the sentence that names what a device loss would look like if one were seen. A prose file that names the marker is matched by a marker scan, so it made the lane red without a run behind it. Excluded by name rather than by rewording the prediction: a document must be free to name the thing it predicts, and a detector that forces its own subject matter out of the project's writing is a detector shaping the evidence. Owner is mine because the file is mine. If a future prediction document does the same, add it here rather than softening the language.

Tank's ctx-4096 device-loss gate, 2026-08-04, arm A (uncapped baseline, resident lane, --steps 8 --seed-past 4096, DEVICE_MEMORY=1, BIND_OUTPUTS=1, KV_ARENA off) on the canonical proof frame: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU running the real Foundry Phi-3.5 model. Three losses in five repetitions — this artifact IS the reproduction, and it is the evidence for `device_memory_flip_blocker_ctx4096_device_loss` in ci/open_reds_device.json, which is open and owned. Provenance and the per-arm reading are in bench/results/device_loss_gate/README.md; the external witness is nvlddmkm Event Id 153 at the same second, so the cause is the driver's unified-memory paging path and not this EP's footprint (alloc_high_water_bytes is constant across losing and clean repetitions). Recorded here on 2026-08-07 under issue #24: it landed committed at 5353886 with no record, and every lane run since has been red on it. Excluding it does NOT close the red — the red is in the device register with its own owner. The both-lanes roll-up of the same 2026-08-04 gate: it re-quotes the captured stderr of the losing repetitions, in raw and JSON-escaped UTF-16LE form, which is why its witness count is the largest in this file. No reading is differenced from it; it is the record.

THIRD device loss on this project, 2026-08-03, and the artifact of it. Found not by me but by ci/check_device_loss.py --lane after I had already read this file and reported its failure as `alloc_device failed for input buffer` — I read the allocation text, stopped, and missed a lost device in the same stderr. The line is `vkQueueSubmit failed: The logical device has been lost`, twice, from cmd.rs:235. It is the FIRST (three-lane, pre-fix) concurrency run, taken before this round's queue submit lock existed. Its call site is vkQueueSubmit, which matches the earlier Intel incident in bench/results/trinity-suite-dev1.log and NOT Tank's ctx-512 loss (vkWaitForFences). vkQueueSubmit lists its `queue` parameter as externally synchronized and nothing in this EP provided that synchronization while two sessions on two threads shared one queue, so an unsynchronized submit from two threads is a mechanism that predicts exactly this call site. That is an argument, not a proof: 6 pre-fix and 6 post-fix rounds both show zero further losses, so the loss rate does not discriminate and the fix is justified by the specification rather than by this file. Kept as the record of the state before the lock.

Switch's ctx-4096 KV-chain incident record, 2026-08-03 23:41:42, resident lane on device 0 — NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU, real Foundry Phi-3.5 — matched second-for-second by nvlddmkm Event Id 153. It is the signature run of the same ctx-4096 class Tank later reproduced on demand, and it is load-bearing twice over: ci/negative_control_device_loss.py replays it with its ASCII traceback removed to prove this check sees ORT's UTF-16LE line inside a JSON string, and ci/check_device_loss.py::json_embedded_text quotes it as the artifact that measured that blindness. Recorded here on 2026-08-07 under issue #24; the control names it explicitly on the command line, which overrides this exclusion, so the replayed red arm still reads it.

SECOND, EARLIER device loss, found by this check on 2026-08-02 and not previously reported as one: line 3216, 2026-07-31 10:00:04, Intel (dev1), 'vkQueueSubmit failed: The logical device has been lost' inside test_phi35.py:784. It surfaced only as an AssertionError and was read as a test failure, not as a lost device. It predates the GQA attention change and comes through a different call site (vkQueueSubmit, not vkWaitForFences), so the class is not one kernel's bug and the reporting defect outlives whatever Switch fixes. Routed to Switch with the cause; kept here as the record.

The counters half of the same fourth device loss: `device_losses: 1`, `compute_failures: 1`, `broken_commitments: 1`, `dispatches_executed: 0`, `outputs_bind_declined: 65`, and uploads=1/readbacks=0 — an inference caught in flight, which is what this check's structural rule reports and it is right to. `running_device_names` reads `NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU`, so this is canonical-frame evidence and must not be regenerated on other hardware. Excluded as the record of a loss already gated by its own producer, not as a truncation anyone is allowed to difference: the reading is refused upstream by test_validation_phi35.py.

FOURTH device loss on record, and the artifact of it: Trinity's criterion 3(a) probe (tests/ops/probe_validation_phi35.py), liveness arm, device selector UNSET, on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU over the real Foundry Phi-3.5. The Vulkan validation layer reported `vkWaitForFences(): Returned error VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST` and the child still exited 0 with a complete counters file — the exact shape docs/PLATFORMS.md §7.19.3 names as the reason `device_losses == 0` is gated before any reading from this probe is believed. Nothing downstream consumed it: tests/ops/test_validation_phi35.py raises InstrumentError on `device_losses != 0`, so this arm is an ERROR(instrument), never a PASS, and the criterion 3(a) witnesses on file are the dev0/dev1 arms. Recorded here on 2026-08-07 under issue #24 — the artifact was committed at fb5f0b28 with no record and has made the lane screen red ever since.
